  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env sh

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./rate_shift_type.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1, --ntasks=1     -> -N 1 -n 1
#   --cpus-per-task=100       -> -c 100
#   --mem-per-cpu=4GB         -> (not translated; see note)
#   --output/--error          -> (not translated; see note)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 100 --wrap "sh $0 __flux_inner")

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  shift

  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=rate_shift_type not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-type/--mail-user not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=4GB not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output/--error not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: stdout/stderr will follow Flux defaults unless configured at submission.

  # NOTE: Slurm --qos=low_prio_res not translated.
  # Performance implication: job priority/time limits associated with the QoS will not be applied; scheduling behavior may change.

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=krypton not translated.

  module load R/4.3.2 gnu openblas

  export R_HOME="/opt/cres/lib/hpc/gcc7/R/4.2.3/lib64/R"
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/cres/lib/hpc/gcc7/R/4.2.3/lib64/R/lib"

  # Slurm used ${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}; under Flux we use the requested cores-per-task.

  flux run -n 1 -c 100 julia --threads 100 scripts/06_rate_shift_type_inference.jl > logs/rate_shift_type_inference.txt
fi
"
}
